blockers.description: 'sign in sign up still causes full page reload' is reported but not reproducible. Measured soft on every path: landing -> /login -> /register -> /login, both refusal paths, both success paths and sign-out all stayed on ONE document (navCount 1, a window marker survived every hop, RSC fetches 36-73ms). /login and /register share app/(auth)/layout.tsx so only the page segment swaps, and e2e already asserts this and passes. Only lead: the dev log shows a whole-tree hydration mismatch from a client-only `vc-init` class on <body> (Vercel Toolbar or a browser extension), which makes React discard the server HTML and re-render everything — visually identical to a reload, and absent under headless Playwright.
blockers.workaround: Ask the product owner to retry in an incognito window with extensions disabled. If it still reproduces there, the measurements above are wrong and the investigation restarts.

blockers.description: Finding B is unverified. A review agent claims BoardView never remounts across a board-to-board navigation, so retryColumnName survives and a column Retry writes board A's column name onto board B — a silent wrong write. Reading the code suggests it is REFUTED: app/(dashboard)/boards/[boardId]/page.tsx:65 renders <Suspense key={boardId}> around the subtree containing BoardView, which remounts on key change, and carries a comment saying exactly that. The agent said 'the page renders it unkeyed' — it is keyed one level up.
blockers.workaround: Drive it in the running app before dismissing: create two boards, fail a column create on A, navigate to B, and check whether the toast and its Retry survive.

decisions.decision: A blank subtask or column row BLOCKS the submit; consequently both create modals open with ZERO rows instead of the mock's seeded two/one
decisions.rationale: Product owner submitted a task carrying a blank subtask row and reported it as a defect, reversing 04-UI-SPEC.md's dropped-row reading. The row count and the blank-row rule cannot be chosen independently: keeping the seeded rows would open the modal invalid and charge two deletions for every subtask-less task. This also closes defect #2 from the earlier batch, which nobody could reproduce — the screenshot WAS the repro.

decisions.decision: Split isSessionPayload into isUpstreamIdentity (upstream body) and isSessionPayload (our own cookie)
decisions.rationale: One guard was doing two jobs. The backend answers POST /signup with "displayName": null for a nameless account — a shape the generated contract's `displayName?: string` never declares — so demanding a string reported a CREATED account as failed and burned the email address. Every e2e sign-up fixture fills the Name field, which is exactly why it shipped.

decisions.decision: A toast dismisses on a tap anywhere on its card, excluding interactive descendants
decisions.rationale: REVIEW-1 made the create-failure toasts permanent, and at mobile width the card covers the sidebar's + Create New Board control. Retry is excluded because until it fires the toast holds the only copy of the user's typed values, so a body-dismiss firing on Retry would destroy what Retry replays.

decisions.decision: Tailwind must not scan worktree copies of .planning
decisions.rationale: Planning docs write utility classes with literal placeholders; the scanner turns them into unparseable CSS and a stylesheet that fails to parse 500s every dev page. A worktree is scanned as its OWN root, so its .planning is reached through neither the outer .gitignore nor the existing @source rule — meaning local dev broke for as long as any worktree existed, which is now the normal state.

decisions.decision: comments:check runs in the pre-commit hook, not only in CI
decisions.rationale: It failed three separate CI runs in one session, each time on a comment the hook had already let through, and each failure cost a full red run plus the skipped visual and e2e jobs behind it. The hook ran 2 of CI's 11 gate scripts; this closes the cheapest and most frequently hit part of that gap.

next_action: Wire SOPS + age for local secret management, and prove gitleaks still behaves alongside it. Recommended shape: `age-keygen -o ~/.config/sops/age/keys.txt`; commit an encrypted `secrets.enc.env`; launch via `sops exec-env secrets.enc.env 'pnpm dev'`. Expect gitleaks' entropy-based generic-api-key rule to fire on the base64 ciphertext — allowlist the file BY PATH ONLY, and pair that allowlist with a pre-commit assertion that the file really is encrypted (`grep -q 'ENC\[AES256_GCM' secrets.enc.env`), because an allowlisted path is exactly how a plaintext secret later ships silently. Landing this deletes three existing problems: the Read(.env.*) deny, the ~/.claude/bin/seed-worktree-env wrapper, and worktree env seeding entirely (the encrypted file arrives via git).
